translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jingzi day, the King of Ancheng, Xu, returned from Northern Zhou; an edict named him palace attendant, director of the secretariat, and central guard general, with staff appointed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，以安右將軍吳明徹為安南將軍、江州刺史，督眾軍南討。

translations.literal: On dingchou day Wu Mingche, General Who Pacifies the Right, was made General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou, to take overall command of the armies in the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day Wu Mingche, general who pacifies the right, was made general who pacifies the south and inspector of Jiangzhou, commanding the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 甲申，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On jiashen day a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day the throne proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，司空侯安都破留異於桃支嶺，[16]異脫身奔晉安，東陽郡平。

translations.literal: On gengyin day Minister of Works Hou Andu defeated Liu Yi at Peach Branch Ridge; [16] Yi escaped and fled to Jin'an, and Dongyang commandery was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day Hou Andu, minister of works, routed Liu Yi at Peach Branch Ridge; [16] Yi fled to Jin'an, and Dongyang commandery was pacified.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸卯，曲赦東陽郡。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on guimao day, a partial amnesty was granted to Dongyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on guimao day, Dongyang commandery received a partial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，齊遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On yisi day Qi sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day Northern Qi sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 六月景辰，以侍中、中衛將軍安成王頊為驃騎將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jingchen day, the King of Ancheng, Xu, Palace Attendant and Central Guard General, was made Grand General of Cavalry and Inspector of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jingchen day, the King of Ancheng, Xu, palace attendant and central guard general, was made grand general of cavalry and inspector of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以會稽、東陽、臨海、永嘉、新安、新寧、晉安、建安八郡置東揚州。

translations.literal: The eight commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xin'an, Xinning, Jin'an, and Jian'an were grouped to form East Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eight commanderies—Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, Yongjia, Xin'an, Xinning, Jin'an, and Jian'an—were combined into East Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以揚州刺史始興王伯茂為鎮東將軍、東揚州刺史，征北將軍、司空、南徐州刺史侯安都為侍中、征北大將軍。

translations.literal: The King of Shixing, Boma, Inspector of Yangzhou, was made General Who Guards the East and Inspector of East Yangzhou; Hou Andu, General Who Campaigns North, Minister of Works, and Inspector of South Xuzhou, was made Palace Attendant and Grand General Who Campaigns North.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Shixing, Boma, inspector of Yangzhou, became general who guards the east and inspector of East Yangzhou; Hou Andu, general who campaigns north, minister of works, and inspector of South Xuzhou, became palace attendant and grand general who campaigns north.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己丑，皇太子納妃王氏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on jichou day, the crown prince took Lady Wang as consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jichou day, the crown prince married Lady Wang.

sentences.zh: 在位文武賜帛各有差，孝悌力田為父後者賜爵二級。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials in post were each granted silk according to rank; those noted for filial piety, brotherly duty, and farming vigor who were heirs received two ranks of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Serving officials received graded gifts of silk; men honored for filial piety, brotherly conduct, and farming who were family heirs received two ranks of nobility.

sentences.zh: 九月戊辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuchen, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, the new moon of the ninth month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 以侍中、都官尚書到仲舉為尚書右僕射、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant and Minister of Justice Dao Zhongju was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Zhongju, palace attendant and minister of justice, was made right vice director of the masters of writing and governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，周迪請降，詔安成王頊督眾軍以招納之。

translations.literal: On dinghai day Zhou Di requested surrender; an edict ordered the King of Ancheng, Xu, to take overall command of the armies to receive and settle him.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day Zhou Di offered to surrender; an edict ordered the King of Ancheng, Xu, to command the armies that would take him in.

sentences.zh: 是歲，周所立梁王蕭詧死，子巋代立。

translations.literal: That year Xiao Cha, the Liang king installed by Zhou, died, and his son Kui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xiao Cha, the Liang ruler Zhou had set up, died; his son Kui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月景子，干陀利國遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the fourth year, on jingzi day, the state of Gandhara sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the fourth year, on jingzi day, Gandhara sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 甲申，周迪棄城走，閩州刺史陳寶應納之，臨川郡平。

translations.literal: On jiashen day Zhou Di abandoned the city and fled; Minzhou Inspector Chen Baoying received him, and Linchuan commandery was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day Zhou Di abandoned his city and fled; Chen Baoying, inspector of Minzhou, took him in, and Linchuan commandery was pacified.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以平西將軍、郢州刺史章昭達為護軍將軍，仁武將軍、新州刺史華皎進號平南將軍，鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司、高州刺史黃法𣰋為鎮北大將軍、南徐州刺史，安西將軍、領臨川太守周敷為南豫州刺史，中護軍孫瑒為鎮右將軍。

translations.literal: On renchen day Zhang Zhaoda, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, was made Protector General; Hua Jiao, Benevolent and Martial General and Inspector of Xinzhou, was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South; Huang Fahe, General Who Guards the South with staff equal to the three counsellors and Inspector of Gaozhou, was made Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou; Zhou Fu, General Who Pacifies the West and concurrent Inspector of Linchuan, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou; and Central Bulwark General Sun Yang was made General Who Guards the Right.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Zhang Zhaoda, general who pacifies the west and inspector of Yingzhou, became protector general; Hua Jiao, benevolent and martial general and inspector of Xinzhou, was promoted to general who pacifies the south; Huang Fahe, general who guards the south with staff equal to the three counsellors and inspector of Gaozhou, became grand general who guards the north and inspector of South Xuzhou; Zhou Fu, general who pacifies the west and concurrent inspector of Linchuan, became inspector of South Yuzhou; and central bulwark general Sun Yang became general who guards the right.

sentences.zh: 罷高州隸入江州。

translations.literal: Gaozhou was abolished and merged into Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhou was abolished and placed under Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月戊戌，征南將軍、開府儀同三司、廣州刺史歐陽頠進號征南大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuxu day, Ouyang Yi, General Who Campaigns South with staff equal to the three counsellors and Inspector of Guangzhou, was advanced to Grand General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuxu day, Ouyang Yi, general who campaigns south with staff equal to the three counsellors and inspector of Guangzhou, was promoted to grand general who campaigns south.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以侍中、司空、征北大將軍侯安都為征南大將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengxu day Hou Andu, Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and Grand General Who Campaigns North, was made Grand General Who Campaigns South and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day Hou Andu, palace attendant, minister of works, and grand general who campaigns north, was made grand general who campaigns south and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以平南將軍華皎為南湘州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengshen day Hua Jiao, General Who Pacifies the South, was made Inspector of South Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Hua Jiao, general who pacifies the south, was made inspector of South Xiangzhou.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 17.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note 17.

sentences.zh: 三月辛未，以鎮南將軍、開府儀同三司徐度為侍中、中軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinwei day, Xu Du, General Who Guards the South with staff equal to the three counsellors, was made Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinwei day, Xu Du, general who guards the south with staff equal to the three counsellors, was made palace attendant and grand general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔贈討周迪將士死王事者。

translations.literal: On xinsi day an edict granted posthumous honors to officers and soldiers who died in service campaigning against Zhou Di.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day an edict honored officers and soldiers who fell campaigning against Zhou Di.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛丑，設無遮大會於太極前殿。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on xinchou day, a universal assembly without hindrance was held in the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on xinchou day, a great Buddhist assembly without hindrance was held before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以侍中、中書監、中衛將軍、驃騎將軍、揚州刺史安成王頊為開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On yimao day the King of Ancheng, Xu, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Central Guard General, Grand General of Cavalry, and Inspector of Yangzhou, was given the staff of office equal to the three counsellors.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the King of Ancheng, Xu, palace attendant, director of the secretariat, central guard general, grand general of cavalry, and inspector of Yangzhou, received staff equal to the three counsellors.

sentences.zh: 五月丁卯，安前將軍、右光祿大夫徐世譜卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingmao day, Xu Shipu, General Who Pacifies the Van and Right Director of the Masters of Writing for Splendid Happiness, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingmao day, Xu Shipu, general who pacifies the van and right director of the masters of writing for splendid happiness, died.

sentences.zh: 六月癸巳，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guisi day, the Metal Star was seen in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guisi day, Venus appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 司空侯安都賜死。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Hou Andu was ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Andu, minister of works, was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 七月丁丑，以鎮北大將軍、開府儀同三司、南徐州刺史黃法𣰋為鎮南大將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on dingchou day, Huang Fahe, Grand General Who Guards the North with staff equal to the three counsellors and Inspector of South Xuzhou, was made Grand General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, on dingchou day, Huang Fahe, grand general who guards the north with staff equal to the three counsellors and inspector of South Xuzhou, was made grand general who guards the south and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月壬戌，開府儀同三司、廣州刺史歐陽頠薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renxu day, Ouyang Yi, Grand Mentor with staff equal to the three counsellors and Inspector of Guangzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu day, Ouyang Yi, grand mentor with staff equal to the three counsellors and inspector of Guangzhou, died.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，曲赦京師。

translations.literal: On guihai day a partial amnesty was granted to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day the capital received a partial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 辛未，周迪復寇臨川，詔護軍章昭達率眾討之。

translations.literal: On xinwei day Zhou Di again raided Linchuan; an edict ordered Protector General Zhang Zhaoda to lead the armies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day Zhou Di raided Linchuan again; an edict sent Protector General Zhang Zhaoda against him.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛酉，章昭達大破周迪，悉擒其黨與，迪脫身潛竄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinyou day, Zhang Zhaoda inflicted a great defeat on Zhou Di, captured all his partisans, and Di himself slipped away in secret flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinyou day, Zhang Zhaoda routed Zhou Di, seized his whole following, and Di escaped in hiding.

sentences.zh: 十二月景申，大赦天下。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jingshen day, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jingshen day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 詔護軍將軍章昭達進軍建安，以討陳寶應。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Protector General Zhang Zhaoda to advance the army into Jian'an to attack Chen Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Protector General Zhang Zhaoda to march on Jian'an against Chen Baoying.

sentences.zh: 信威將軍、益州刺史余孝頃督會稽、東陽、臨海、永嘉諸軍自東道會之。

translations.literal: Yu Xiaoxiang, Trustworthy and Martial General and Inspector of Yizhou, was to take overall command of the armies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, and Yongjia from the eastern route to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xiaoxiang, trustworthy and martial general and inspector of Yizhou, was to command Kuaiji, Dongyang, Linhai, and Yongjia troops from the east to link up with him.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以前安南將軍、江州刺史吳明徹為鎮前將軍。

translations.literal: On guichou day the former General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou, Wu Mingche, was made General Who Guards the Van.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Wu Mingche, former general who pacifies the south and inspector of Jiangzhou, was made general who guards the van.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月庚辰，以吏部尚書、領右軍將軍袁樞為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the fifth year, on gengchen day, Yuan Shu, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrent General of the Right Army, was made Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the fifth year, on gengchen day, Yuan Shu, minister of the ministry of personnel and general of the right army, was made governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，輿駕親祠北郊。

translations.literal: On xinsi day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the emperor sacrificed in person at the Northern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，江州湓城火，燒死者二百餘人。

translations.literal: On yiyou day a fire broke out at Pencheng in Jiangzhou; more than two hundred people died in the blaze.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day fire destroyed Pencheng in Jiangzhou, killing more than two hundred people.

sentences.zh: 三月丁丑，以征南大將軍、開府儀同三司、桂州刺史淳于量為中撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on dingchou day, Chunyu Liang, Grand General Who Campaigns South with staff equal to the three counsellors and Inspector of Guizhou, was made Grand General Who Pacifies the Center.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on dingchou day, Chunyu Liang, grand general who campaigns south with staff equal to the three counsellors and inspector of Guizhou, was made grand general who pacifies the center.

sentences.zh: 壬午，詔以故護軍將軍周鐵虎配食高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: On renwu day an edict ordered the late Protector General Zhou Tiehu to receive offerings in the Founder Emperor's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day an edict placed the late Protector General Zhou Tiehu in the roster of sacrifices at the Founder Emperor's temple.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚子，周遣使來聘。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on gengzi day, Zhou sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on gengzi day, Northern Zhou sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 五月庚午，罷南丹陽郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on gengwu day, South Danyang commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on gengwu day, South Danyang commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 是月，周、齊並遣使來聘。

translations.literal: That month Zhou and Qi both sent envoys on friendly missions.
translations.idiomatic: That month both Northern Zhou and Northern Qi sent friendly embassies.

sentences.zh: 六月丁未，夜，有白氣兩道，出于北斗東南，屬地。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingwei day, at night, two white vapors issued southeast of the Northern Dipper and reached the ground.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of dingwei in the sixth month, two white rays rose southeast of the Big Dipper and touched the earth.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁丑，詔曰：「朕以寡昧，屬當負重，星籥亟改，冕旒弗曠，不能仰協璿衡，用調玉燭，傍慰蒼生，以安黔首。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on dingchou day, an edict said: "We, being slight and dull, have been set to bear a heavy burden; the year's markers change in quick succession, yet We do not neglect the imperial cap; We cannot look up to harmonize the celestial balance, use it to tune the jade measure, and by that means comfort the blue-clad people and settle the black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on dingchou day, an edict declared: "We are unworthy yet bear the throne; years turn quickly, yet We never neglect the crown. We cannot align Heaven's scale, adjust the jade tally, and so comfort the people and give the masses peace.

sentences.zh: 兵無寧歲，民乏有年，移風之道未弘，習俗之患猶在，致令氓多觸網，吏繁筆削，獄犴滋章，雖由物犯，囹圄淹滯，亦或有冤。

translations.literal: The armies know no year of rest, the people lack years of plenty; the way of shifting customs is not yet broadly spread, the harm of entrenched habits still remains, so that the common folk often touch the net, clerks multiply brush-and-knife work, prisons and cages grow more numerous—though this comes from things offending the law, yet in the jails the detained linger long, and among them there are also the wrongly accused.
translations.idiomatic: War gives the land no quiet year; the people know lean harvests. Reform has not gone far enough, old abuses remain, and too many commoners fall into the law. Clerks multiply their records; prisons swell. Some suffer through their own crimes, but many linger in chains who may be innocent.

sentences.zh: 念俾納隍，載勞負扆，加以膚湊不適，攝衛有虧，比獲微痊，思覃寬惠，可曲赦京師。」

translations.literal: Thinking how the people are like those about to fall into the moat, We toil at the throne-back screen; moreover Our skin and flesh are ill at ease and Our regimen of care is impaired; having lately obtained slight recovery, We wish to spread broad mercy—a partial amnesty may be granted to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Remembering the people on the brink of ruin, We labor at the throne; Our health too has failed and Our care of the body is wanting. Now that We are somewhat recovered, We mean to show wide mercy: let the capital receive a partial amnesty."

sentences.zh: 九月，城西城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the western city was walled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month work walled the western quarter of the capital.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月丁亥，以左衛將軍程靈洗為中護軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on dinghai day, Cheng Lingxi, General of the Left Guard, was made Central Bulwark General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, on dinghai day, Cheng Lingxi, general of the left guard, was made central bulwark general.

sentences.zh: 己丑，章昭達破陳寶應于建安，擒寶應、留異，送京師，晉安郡平。

translations.literal: On jichou day Zhang Zhaoda defeated Chen Baoying at Jian'an, captured Baoying and Liu Yi, and sent them to the capital; Jin'an commandery was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Zhang Zhaoda defeated Chen Baoying at Jian'an, seized Baoying and Liu Yi, and sent them to the capital; Jin'an commandery was pacified.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以護軍將軍章昭達為鎮前將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On jiachen day Protector General Zhang Zhaoda was made General Who Guards the Van with staff equal to the three counsellors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day Protector General Zhang Zhaoda was made general who guards the van with staff equal to the three counsellors.

sentences.zh: 十二月甲子，曲赦建安、晉安二郡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiazi day, a partial amnesty was granted to Jian'an and Jin'an commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiazi day, Jian'an and Jin'an commanderies received a partial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 討陳寶應將士死王事者，並給棺槥，送還本鄉，并復其家。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers who died in service campaigning against Chen Baoying were all provided coffins and sent back to their native districts, and their families were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers who fell against Chen Baoying were given coffins and sent home, and their families were restored to standing.

sentences.zh: 瘡痍未瘳者，給其醫藥。

translations.literal: Those whose wounds were not yet healed were given medicine.
translations.idiomatic: The wounded who had not yet recovered were supplied with medicine.

sentences.zh: 癸未，齊遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On guiwei day Qi sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Northern Qi sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月甲午，皇太子加元服，王公以下賜帛各有差，孝悌力田為父後者賜爵一級，鰥寡孤獨不能自存者穀人五斛。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the sixth year, on jiawu day, the crown prince received the capping of adulthood; kings, dukes, and those below were each granted silk according to rank; those noted for filial piety, brotherly duty, and farming vigor who were heirs received one rank of nobility; widows, orphans, and the solitary who could not support themselves received five hu of grain per person.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the sixth year, on jiawu day, the crown prince came of age; princes and officials received graded gifts of silk; filial farmers who were heirs gained one rank of nobility; and widows, orphans, and the destitute received five hu of grain each.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以領軍將軍杜稜為翊左將軍、丹陽尹，丹陽尹袁樞為吏部尚書，衛尉卿沈欽為中領軍。

translations.literal: On gengxu day Du Ling, General of the Garrison Army, was made Left Assistant General and Governor of Danyang; Yuan Shu, Governor of Danyang, was made Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; and Shen Qin, Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues, was made General of the Garrison Army.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day Du Ling, general of the garrison army, became left assistant general and governor of Danyang; Yuan Shu, governor of Danyang, became minister of the ministry of personnel; and Shen Qin, chamberlain for the palace revenues, became general of the garrison army.

sentences.zh: 三月乙未，詔侯景以來遭亂移在建安、晉安、義安郡者，並許還本土，其被略為奴婢者，釋為良民。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yiwei day, an edict said that from the time of Hou Jing's rebellion onward, those displaced by disorder and moved into Jian'an, Jin'an, and Yi'an commanderies were all permitted to return to their native places; those seized and made slaves or bondmaids were released as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yiwei day, an edict allowed everyone displaced since Hou Jing's rebellion into Jian'an, Jin'an, and Yi'an to go home, and ordered those taken as slaves or bondmaids freed as commoners.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲寅，以侍中、中書監、中衛將軍、驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史安成王頊為司空。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on jiayin day, the King of Ancheng, Xu, Palace Attendant, Director of the Secretariat, Central Guard General, Grand General of Cavalry with staff equal to the three counsellors, and Inspector of Yangzhou, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jiayin day, the King of Ancheng, Xu, palace attendant, director of the secretariat, central guard general, grand general of cavalry with staff equal to the three counsellors, and inspector of Yangzhou, was made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，有彗星見。

translations.literal: On xinyou day a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day a comet was seen.

sentences.zh: [18]周遣使來聘。

translations.literal: [18] Zhou sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: [18] Northern Zhou sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸未，大風至自西南，廣百餘步，激壞靈臺候樓。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on guiwei day, a great wind came from the southwest, more than a hundred paces wide, and struck and destroyed the Spirit Terrace observation tower.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on guiwei day, a gale from the southwest, over a hundred paces across, wrecked the Spirit Terrace watchtower.

sentences.zh: 甲申，儀賢堂無故自壞。

translations.literal: On jiashen day the Hall for Honoring the Worthy collapsed for no apparent reason.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day the Hall for Honoring the Worthy collapsed without evident cause.

sentences.zh: 景戌，臨川太守駱文牙斬周迪，[19]傳首京師，梟於朱雀航。

translations.literal: On jingxu day Linchuan Governor Luo Wenya beheaded Zhou Di; [19] the head was sent to the capital and exposed at the Vermilion Bird landing.
translations.idiomatic: On jingxu day Luo Wenya, governor of Linchuan, executed Zhou Di; [19] the head was sent to the capital and displayed at the Vermilion Bird landing.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On dingyou day the Metal Star was seen in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Venus appeared by day.

sentences.zh: 八月丁丑，詔曰：「梁室多故，禍亂相尋，兵甲紛紜，十年不解，不逞之徒虐流生氣，無賴之屬暴及徂魂。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dingchou day, an edict said: "The House of Liang suffered many troubles; calamity followed calamity; armor and weapons were in turmoil for ten years without respite; unbridled men vented cruelty on the living breath, and worthless sorts brought violence even upon the departed souls.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingchou day, an edict declared: "The Liang house knew endless trouble; disaster followed disaster; arms did not rest for ten years; the lawless ravaged the living, and the vile afflicted the dead.

sentences.zh: 江左肇基，王者攸宅，金行水位之主，木運火德之君，時更四代，歲逾二百。

translations.literal: When the southeast first laid its foundations, it was the dwelling of kings; rulers of the Metal phase and Water phase, and sovereigns of the Wood phase and Fire phase, in all four successions, for more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: When the southeast first rose, it was the seat of kings—sovereigns of metal and water, wood and fire, four lines in all, spanning more than two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 若其經綸

translations.literal: As for their weaving the realm
translations.idiomatic: In ordering the realm

translations.literal: (three)
translations.idiomatic: (three)

sentences.zh: 〔王〕業，[20]縉紳民望，忠臣孝子，何世無才，[21]而零落山丘，變移陵谷，或皆剪伐，莫不侵殘。

translations.literal: [wang] enterprise, [20] the gentry's esteem and the people's hope, loyal ministers and filial sons—what age lacks talent? [21] Yet they lie scattered on the hills, tombs and valleys have shifted, or all were cut down—none escaped violation and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: [wang] enterprise, [20] the gentry's honor and the people's hope—loyal ministers and filial sons appear in every age, [21] yet they lie ruined on the hills, graves and valleys have shifted, and many were cut down until nothing was left unspoiled.

sentences.zh: 玉杯得於民間，漆簡傳於世載，無復五株之樹，罕見千年之表。

translations.literal: Jade cups were obtained among the people, lacquered documents passed down through generations, but there were no longer trees of five trunks, and tables a thousand years old were rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: Jade cups survived among the people and lacquered books in family stores, but the five-trunk trees were gone and thousand-year tablets seldom seen.

sentences.zh: 自大祚光啟，恭惟揖讓，爰暨朕躬，聿脩祖武，雖復旂旗服色，猶行杞、宋之

translations.literal: From the time the great mandate brightly opened, reverently yielding the throne down to Our own person, We have continued the ancestral martial way; though banners, flags, and dress still follow the states of Qi and Song,
translations.idiomatic: Since the great mandate dawned, from the reverent yielding of the throne down to Our own reign, We have kept the ancestral way; though banners and dress still follow the model of Qi and Song,

translations.literal: (plan)
translations.idiomatic: (plan)

sentences.zh: 〔邦〕，[22]每車駕巡遊，眇瞻河、雒之路，故喬山之祀，蘋藻弗虧，驪山之墳，松柏恆守。

translations.literal: [state], [22] whenever the imperial carriage tours, We gaze from afar on the roads to the Yellow River and Luo; therefore the sacrifices at Mount Qiao are not neglected, water-chestnut and pondweed are not wanting, and at Mount Li's tombs the pines and cypresses are ever kept.
translations.idiomatic: [state], [22] whenever We tour, We look toward the Yellow River and Luo; the rites at Mount Qiao are not neglected, offerings are not wanting, and at Mount Li the pines and cypresses stand guard.

sentences.zh: 唯戚藩舊壟，士子故塋，掩殣未周，樵牧猶眾。

translations.literal: Only the old mounds of imperial kinsmen and the former graves of scholars and officers were not fully covered in burial; woodcutters and herdsmen still thronged them.
translations.idiomatic: Only the old tombs of imperial kin and the graves of scholars and officers were not fully tended; woodcutters and herdsmen still swarmed there.

sentences.zh: 或親屬流隸，負土無期，子孫冥滅，手植何寄。

translations.literal: Some kinsmen were cast into bondage and could find no day to heap the earth; descendants perished in obscurity, and the trees they planted with their own hands had no one to keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Some kin were sold into bondage and could not mound the earth in time; lines died out in silence, and the trees they planted had no keeper.

sentences.zh: 漢高留連於無忌，宋祖惆悵於子房，丘墓生哀，性靈共惻者也。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu lingered in grief at Wuji's tomb, and the Song founder was filled with sorrow at Zifang's grave—tombs can stir pity, and the inner heart shares the ache.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu mourned at Wuji's tomb, and the Song founder grieved at Zhang Liang's grave—tombs move the heart, and spirit feels the same sorrow.

sentences.zh: [23]朕所以興言永日，思慰幽泉。

translations.literal: [23] This is why We speak all day and think to comfort the dark springs.
translations.idiomatic: [23] That is why We speak of it through the day and wish to comfort the dead below.

sentences.zh: 維前代王侯，自古忠烈，墳冢被髮絕無後者，可檢行脩治，墓中樹木，勿得樵採，庶幽顯咸暢，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: As for former dynasties' kings and marquises, and loyal and fierce men of old whose tombs were disheveled and utterly without heirs, an inspection may be made and repairs carried out; trees within the tombs must not be cut for fuel or gathered—so that the hidden and the manifest may alike be at ease, in accord with Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Former kings and marquises, and loyal and fierce men of old whose graves lie ruined and without heirs, shall be sought out and repaired; trees in the tombs must not be cut for fuel—so that the living and the dead may be at peace, as We desire."

sentences.zh: 」己卯，立皇子伯固為新安郡王，伯恭為晉安王，伯仁為廬陵王，伯義為江夏王。

translations.literal: On jimao day the princes Bogu, Bogong, Boren, and Boyi were enfeoffed as Kings of Xin'an, Jin'an, Luling, and Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Princes Bogu, Bogong, Boren, and Boyi were enfeoffed as kings of Xin'an, Jin'an, Luling, and Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 九月癸未，罷豫章郡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guiwei day, Yuzhang commandery was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guiwei day, Yuzhang commandery was abolished.

sentences.zh: 是月，新作大航。

translations.literal: That month a new Great Floating Bridge was built.
translations.idiomatic: That month a new Great Floating Bridge was constructed.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛亥，齊遣使來聘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on xinhai day, Qi sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on xinhai day, Northern Qi sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙卯，立皇子伯禮為武陵王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yimao day, the Prince of Wuling, Boli, was enfeoffed as king.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yimao day, Prince Boli was enfeoffed as King of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以鎮前將軍、開府儀同三司章昭達為鎮南將軍、江州刺史，鎮南大將軍、江州刺史黃法𣰋為中衛大將軍，中護軍程靈洗為宣毅將軍、郢州刺史，軍師將軍、郢州刺史沈恪為中護軍，鎮東將軍、吳興太守吳明徹為中領軍。

translations.literal: On dingsi day Zhang Zhaoda, General Who Guards the Van with staff equal to the three counsellors, was made Grand General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou; Huang Fahe, Grand General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou, was made Grand Central Guard General; Cheng Lingxi, Central Bulwark General, was made Trustworthy and Martial General and Inspector of Yingzhou; Shen Ke, Military Adviser General and Inspector of Yingzhou, was made Central Bulwark General; and Wu Mingche, General Who Guards the East and Governor of Wuxing, was made General of the Garrison Army.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day Zhang Zhaoda, general who guards the van with staff equal to the three counsellors, became grand general who guards the south and inspector of Jiangzhou; Huang Fahe, grand general who guards the south and inspector of Jiangzhou, became grand central guard general; Cheng Lingxi, central bulwark general, became trustworthy and martial general and inspector of Yingzhou; Shen Ke, military adviser general and inspector of Yingzhou, became central bulwark general; and Wu Mingche, general who guards the east and governor of Wuxing, became general of the garrison army.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以東中郎將、吳郡太守鄱陽王伯山為平北將軍、南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: On wuwu day the King of Poyang, Boshan, Eastern Central Commander and Governor of Wu commandery, was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day the King of Poyang, Boshan, eastern central commander and governor of Wu commandery, was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔曰：「朕自居民牧之重，託在王公之上，顧其寡昧，鬱于治道。

translations.literal: On guihai day an edict said: "Since We undertook the heavy charge of nurturing the people and were set above kings and dukes, We have seen Our own dullness and been troubled in the way of rule.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day an edict declared: "Since We took on the burden of caring for the people and were set above kings and dukes, We have known Our own dullness and been troubled at governing.

sentences.zh: 加以屢虧聽覽，事多壅積，冤滯靡申，幽枉弗鑒。

translations.literal: Moreover We have repeatedly impaired Our hearing and sight; affairs have piled up in obstruction; grievances held in detention are not cleared, and the hidden and wronged are not examined.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again Our health has failed; business has piled up blocked; prisoners' grievances go unheard, and hidden wrongs are not judged.

sentences.zh: 念茲罪隸，有甚納隍。

translations.literal: Thinking of these who bear guilt and fetters, it is like those about to fall into the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of those in chains, We feel as though the people stood on the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 而惠澤未流，愆陽累月，今歲序云暮，元正向肇，欲使幽圄之內，同被時和，可曲赦京師。」

translations.literal: Yet Our favor has not flowed forth; for successive months the yang has been out of balance; now the year's sequence draws to its end and the new year is about to begin—We wish those within the dark prisons likewise to share the season's harmony; a partial amnesty may be granted to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Yet mercy has not gone out; drought has lingered for months. The year ends and the new year nears—We wish even those in prison to share the season's peace: let the capital receive a partial amnesty."

sentences.zh: 天康元年春二月景子，詔曰：「朕以寡德，纂承洪緒，日昃劬勞，思弘景業，而政道多昧，黎庶未康，兼疹患淹時，亢陽累月，百姓何咎，寔由朕躬，念茲在茲，痛如疾首。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring of the first year of Tiankang, on jingzi day, an edict said: "We, being slight in virtue, have succeeded to the great succession; from sun to sun We toil, thinking to expand the bright enterprise—yet the way of government is much obscure, the black-haired masses are not yet at ease; moreover Our illness has lingered long, and drought has piled up for months; what fault is it of the common people? Truly it lies in Our own person; thinking of this, thinking of this, the pain is like a wound in the head.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring of the first year of Tiankang, on jingzi day, an edict declared: "We are unworthy yet have inherited the great line. Day and night We labor to enlarge the bright work, yet government is still unclear and the people are not at ease. Illness has lingered, drought has lasted for months—the people are blameless; the fault is Ours alone. The thought of it pains Us like a wound in the head.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下，改天嘉七年為天康元年。」

translations.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed throughout the realm; the seventh year of Tianjia is changed to the first year of Tiankang."
translations.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty, and let the seventh year of Tianjia become the first year of Tiankang."

sentences.zh: 三月己卯，以驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史、司空安成王頊為尚書令。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jimao day, the King of Ancheng, Xu, Grand General of Cavalry with staff equal to the three counsellors and Inspector of Yangzhou and Minister of Works, was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jimao day, the King of Ancheng, Xu, grand general of cavalry with staff equal to the three counsellors, inspector of Yangzhou, and minister of works, was made director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙卯，皇孫至澤生，在位文武賜絹帛各有差，為父後者賜爵一級。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on yimao day, an imperial grandson, Ze, was born; civil and military officials in post were each granted silk and brocade according to rank; heirs received one rank of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on yimao day, an imperial grandson, Ze, was born; officials received graded gifts of silk and brocade, and heirs one rank of nobility.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，世祖疾甚。

translations.literal: On guiyou day Emperor Wen's illness grew severe.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day Emperor Wen's illness grew critical.

sentences.zh: 是日，崩于有覺殿。

translations.literal: That day, he died at the Hall of Awakening Consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he died in Youjue Hall.

sentences.zh: 遺詔曰：「朕疾苦彌留，遂至不救，脩短有命，夫復何言。

translations.literal: The testament edict said: "I am ill and lingering near death, reaching the point of no recovery; long and short life have their allotted span—what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: His death edict read: "My illness lingers without relief and has reached what medicine cannot cure; length of days is ordained—what more can I say?

sentences.zh: 但王業艱難，頻歲軍旅，生民多弊，無忘愧惕。

translations.literal: Only the royal enterprise is arduous; year after year there are campaigns; the living people are much afflicted—do not forget shame and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the throne's work is hard, campaigns come year after year, and the people bear many wounds—never lose your sense of shame and care.

sentences.zh: 今方隅乃定，俗教未弘，便及大漸，以為遺恨。

translations.literal: Now the regions are only just settled, popular teaching is not yet spread abroad, and I meet the great decline—it is a regret left behind.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has only just been pacified and custom and learning are not yet abroad, yet I approach my end—that is my regret.

sentences.zh: 社稷任重，太子可即君臨，王侯將相，善相輔翊，內外協和，勿違朕意！

translations.literal: The altars of soil and grain bear heavy responsibility; the Crown Prince may immediately assume rule; kings, marquises, generals, and ministers—well assist and support; inner and outer in harmony—do not go against my intent!
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on heavy shoulders: let the crown prince take the throne at once; let princes and ministers aid him well; keep court and command united and do not stray from my wish.

sentences.zh: 山陵務存儉速。

translations.literal: The mountain tomb should be kept frugal and swift.
translations.idiomatic: Keep my tomb plain and the burial swift.

sentences.zh: 大斂竟，群臣三日一臨，公除之制，率依舊典。」

translations.literal: When the great encoffining is finished, the hundred officials shall attend once every three days; the regulations for removing public mourning—all follow the old statutes."
translations.idiomatic: After the laying in state, ministers shall attend every three days; rules for ending public mourning shall follow the old code."

sentences.zh: 六月甲子，群臣上謚曰文皇帝，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi day, the hundred officials presented the posthumous title Emperor Wen, temple name Shizu (Founding Ancestor).
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi day, the ministers offered the posthumous name Emperor Wen and temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 景寅，葬永寧陵。

translations.literal: On jingyin day, he was buried at Yongning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jingyin day he was interred at Yongning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 世祖起自艱難，知百姓疾苦。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen rose from hardship and knew the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen came up through hardship and understood the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 國家資用，務從儉約。

translations.literal: State expenditures strove for thrift and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: State spending was kept spare and frugal.

sentences.zh: 常所調斂，事不獲已者，必咨嗟改色，若在諸身。

translations.literal: In regular levies and collections, when affairs could not be avoided, he would surely sigh and change countenance, as if upon his own person.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever unavoidable levies had to be ordered, he sighed and his face fell as if the burden were his own.

sentences.zh: 主者奏決，妙識真偽，下不容姦，人知自勵矣。

translations.literal: When the responsible official presented decisions, he finely discerned truth and falsehood; below him deceit found no place, and people knew to encourage themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed memorials with a keen eye for truth and fraud; subordinates could not cheat, and men learned to discipline themselves.

sentences.zh: 一夜內刺閨取外事分判者，前後相續。

translations.literal: In one night those who pierced the inner quarters to fetch external affairs for separate judgment came one after another without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Night after night messengers came from the inner gate bearing outside business for him to decide.

sentences.zh: 每雞人伺漏，傳更籤於殿中，乃敕送者必投籤於階石之上，令鎗然有聲，云「吾雖眠，亦令驚覺也」。

translations.literal: Whenever the cock herald waited on the clepsydra and passed the night tally into the hall, he then ordered the deliverer to cast the tally upon the step-stone so that it rang with a clang, saying, "Though I sleep, I shall also be made to start awake."
translations.idiomatic: Each time the night herald brought the watch tally to the hall, he ordered it thrown onto the stone steps with a sharp clatter, saying, "Even in sleep I want to be roused."

sentences.zh: 始終梗概，若此者多焉。

translations.literal: From beginning to end his stern integrity—such instances were many.
translations.idiomatic: His firm character showed in many such ways from first to last.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：世稱繼體守文，宗枝承統，得失之閒，蓋亦詳矣。

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: The world speaks of succeeding the bodily succession and guarding the written canon, of collateral branches inheriting the line—the gaps between gain and loss, it may be said, are also fully set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Chen Director of the Ministry of Personnel, said: The world judges heirs who keep the founder's way and branches that carry on the line, and the record of success and failure is long.

sentences.zh: 大抵以奉而勿墜為賢能，橈而易之為不肖；

translations.literal: In general, to uphold and not let fall is deemed worthy ability; to bend and easily change it is deemed unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: In general, to hold the legacy without letting it slip counts as talent; to warp or lightly change it counts as failure.

sentences.zh: 其有光揚前軌，克荷曾構，固以少焉。

translations.literal: Those who can glorify the former track and bear the weight of what ancestors built are indeed few.
translations.idiomatic: Those who brighten their forebears' path and bear up the work of earlier builders are few indeed.

sentences.zh: 世祖自初發跡，功庸顯著，寧亂靜寇，首佐大業。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen from his first setting forth, merit and achievement were conspicuous; he pacified disorder and quieted marauders, first assisting the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: From his first rise Emperor Wen's deeds were plain: he stilled rebellion, quieted enemies, and stood at the head of the founding effort.

sentences.zh: 及國禍奄臻，入承寶祚，兢兢業業，其若馭朽。

translations.literal: When the state's calamity suddenly arrived, he entered to receive the precious throne, cautious and fearful, as if driving rotten wood.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck the realm and he took the throne, he was cautious and uneasy, as one who drives a rotted axle.

sentences.zh: [24]加以崇尚儒術，愛悅文義，見善如弗及，用人如由己，恭儉以御身，勤勞以濟物，自昔允文允武之君，東征西怨之后，賓實之跡，可為聯類。

translations.literal: [24] Moreover he revered Confucian learning, loved and delighted in literary principle, saw good as if he could not reach it, employed men as if through himself, used respectful frugality to govern his person and diligence to aid things—of old the paragons of civil and martial virtue, the queens who sighed east and west on campaign—the traces of guest and essence could be joined in kind.
translations.idiomatic: [24] He honored Confucian learning and loved letters, pursued good as if he could never catch it, and chose men as if for himself; he ruled his own life with modest frugality and labored for the people's good. He belongs in the company of rulers true in wen and wu and of consorts whose campaigns won both praise and lament—the pattern fits the finest models of old.

sentences.zh: 至於杖聰明，用鑒識，斯則永平之政，前史其論諸。

translations.literal: As for wielding intelligence and employing discernment, that is the government of Yongping—the former histories have discussed it in those terms.
translations.idiomatic: In wielding talent and sound judgment he matched the Yongping reign of Han; the histories say as much.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 以功授持節都督會稽等十郡諸軍事宣毅將軍會稽太守 按高祖紀下永定元年十一月丙申詔文，「持節」作「使持節」。

translations.literal: By merit he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Area Commander over ten commanderies including Kuaiji, General Who Proclaims Martial Valor, and Governor of Kuaiji—comment: in the edict text of the Basic Annals of the Founder, Part Two, for the bingchen day of the eleventh month of the first year of Yongding, "Bearer of the Staff" reads "Bearer of the Staff with Credential."
translations.idiomatic: On "by merit appointed Bearer of the Staff, commander of ten Kuaiji-region commanderies, General Who Proclaims Martial Valor, governor of Kuaiji": the Founder's annals for Yongding 1/11/bingchen read Bearer of the Staff with Credential.

sentences.zh: 別有長城縣侯之爵，此未書。

translations.literal: Separately there was the rank of Marquis of Changcheng County; this is not written here.
translations.idiomatic: He also held the rank of Marquis of Changcheng County, omitted here.

sentences.zh: 平南將軍開府儀同三司周迪進號鎮南將軍 按

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South, Opener of the Mansion with Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Zhou Di was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons the South—comment:
translations.idiomatic: On "General Who Pacifies the South, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes Zhou Di advanced to General Who Garrisons the South"—note:

sentences.zh: 〈周迪傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Zhou Di〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Zhou Di〉

sentences.zh: 「鎮南將軍」作「安南將軍」。

translations.literal: "General Who Garrisons the South" reads "General Who Pacifies the South."
translations.idiomatic: reads General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 庚戌封皇子伯茂為始興王 按

translations.literal: On gengxu day Prince Bamao was enfeoffed as Prince of Shixing—comment:
translations.idiomatic: On "gengxu day Prince Bamao was enfeoffed Prince of Shixing"—note:

sentences.zh: 〈始興王伯茂傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Prince Bamao of Shixing〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Prince Bamao of Shixing〉

sentences.zh: ，其受封在永定三年十月，此云八月庚戌，與傳異。

translations.literal: , his receiving the enfeoffment was in the tenth month of the third year of Yongding; here it says the eighth month, gengxu day—it differs from the biography.
translations.idiomatic: his enfeoffment came in the tenth month of Yongding year 3; this entry's eighth month, gengxu day disagrees with the biography.

sentences.zh: 徙封始興嗣王頊為安成王 「頊」原作「諱」，蓋姚察原文如是，今據北監本、汲本、殿本改。

translations.literal: Changing the enfeoffment of the Heir of Shixing, Prince Xu, to Prince of Ancheng: "Xu" originally read "taboo name"—probably Yao Cha's original text was thus; now according to the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions it is changed.
translations.idiomatic: On "transferring the Shixing heir Prince Xu to Prince of Ancheng": the text originally read taboo name, preserving Yao Cha's wording; emended per the Northern Supervisory, Jigu, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 後如此不悉出校記。

translations.literal: Hereafter when such cases occur, collation notes are not all fully given.
translations.idiomatic: Similar cases below are not all noted in full.

sentences.zh: 九月辛酉立皇子伯宗為皇太子 按「九月辛酉」廢帝紀作「八月庚戌」。

translations.literal: On xinyou day of the ninth month Prince Bozong was established as Crown Prince—comment: "ninth month, xinyou day" in the Basic Annals of the Deposed Emperor reads "eighth month, gengxu day."
translations.idiomatic: On "ninth month, xinyou day, Prince Bozong was made crown prince": the Deposed Emperor's annals read eighth month, gengxu day.

sentences.zh: 忭流庶俗 「忭」原訛「抃」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Exultation flowed among the common folk: "exultation" was originally corrupted to "clap hands"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "exultation flowed among the common folk": the text originally read clap for exult; other editions are correct; emended.

sentences.zh: 亦同肆眚 「肆」原訛「拜」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Also alike in bestowing amnesty: "bestow" was originally corrupted to "bow"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "also alike in bestowing amnesty": the text originally read bow for bestow; other editions are correct; emended.

sentences.zh: 江寧既是舊塋 「是」北監本、殿本作「有」。

translations.literal: Jiangning was already the old burial ground: "was"—the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read "had."
translations.idiomatic: On "Jiangning was already the old burial ground": the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions read had for was.

sentences.zh: 使棫樸載哥 「哥」《元龜》八一三作「歌」。

translations.literal: Making oaks and unhewn timber bear songs: "song (ge)"—Yuan Gui 813 reads "song (ge)."
translations.idiomatic: On "making oaks and rough timber bear song": Yuan Gui 813 reads song (ge) instead of brother (ge).

sentences.zh: 按哥即古歌字，下「哥鍾列於管庫」同。

translations.literal: Comment: ge is the ancient character for song; below, "song-bells arrayed in the storehouse treasury" is the same.
translations.idiomatic: Note: ge is the archaic form of song; the same applies to song-bells in the storehouse treasury below.

sentences.zh: 寬網眘刑 「眘」各本作「省」。

translations.literal: Broadening the net and cautious punishment: "cautious"—all editions read "reduce."
translations.idiomatic: On "broadening the net and cautious punishment": all editions read reduce (sheng) for the character here rendered cautious (shen).

sentences.zh: 按眘古慎字，作「省」者疑後人臆改。

translations.literal: Comment: shen is the ancient character for cautious; those who read "reduce" are suspected of later arbitrary emendation.
translations.idiomatic: Note: shen is the old form of cautious; reduce looks like a later guess.

sentences.zh: 遣巴州刺史侯安鼎守之 「侯安鼎」各本作「侯安都」。

translations.literal: Dispatching Ba Province Inspector Hou Anding to garrison it: "Hou Anding"—all editions read "Hou Andu."
translations.idiomatic: On "dispatching Ba Province Inspector Hou Anding to hold it": all editions read Hou Andu.

sentences.zh: 張元濟

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanji
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanji

sentences.zh: 〈校勘記〉

translations.literal: 〈Collation note〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Collation note〉

sentences.zh: 云：「時侯安都以司空會侯瑱南討，未嘗為巴州刺史，侯安鼎當別是一人。」

translations.literal: says: "At the time Hou Andu as Minister of Works joined Hou Tian on the southern campaign and had never been Ba Province inspector—Hou Anding must be a different person."
translations.idiomatic: writes: "At the time Hou Andu as minister of works joined Hou Tian on the southern campaign and had never been Ba Province inspector—Hou Anding must be someone else."

sentences.zh: 合州刺史裴景徽奔于齊 「裴景徽」《北齊書》、《南史·王琳傳》並作「裴景暉」。

translations.literal: He Province Inspector Pei Jinghui fled to Qi: "Pei Jinghui"—the Book of Northern Qi and the Biography of Wang Lin in the History of the Southern Dynasties both read "Pei Jinghui (variant character)."
translations.idiomatic: On "He Province Inspector Pei Jinghui fled to Qi": the Book of Northern Qi and the Wang Lin biography in the Southern Dynasties annals both read Pei Jinghui with a variant final character (hui).

sentences.zh: 丁丑 按是年三月丁未朔，無丁丑，缺疑。

translations.literal: Dingchou day—comment: that year in the third month dingwei was the first day of the month; there was no dingchou; lacuna suspected.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day: that year the third month began on dingwei—no dingchou occurs; date doubtful.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙巳 「乙巳」《南史·陳世祖紀》作「癸丑」。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, yisi day: "yisi"—the Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "guichou."
translations.idiomatic: On "winter, tenth month, yisi day": the Southern Dynasties Annals of Chen Emperor Wen read guichou.

sentences.zh: 按是年十月癸酉朔，無乙巳，亦無癸丑，缺疑。

translations.literal: Comment: that year in the tenth month guiyou was the first day of the month; there was neither yisi nor guichou; lacuna suspected.
translations.idiomatic: That year the tenth month began on guiyou—neither yisi nor guichou fits; date doubtful.

sentences.zh: 天嘉三年，高句驪王高湯，或本作「高陽」。

translations.literal: Tianjia year 3, Goguryeo King Gao Tang—or some editions read "Gao Yang."
translations.idiomatic: Tianjia year 3, Goguryeo king Gao Tang; some texts read Gao Yang.

sentences.zh: 司空侯安都破留異於桃支嶺 「桃支嶺」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Hou Andu defeated Liu Yi at Taozhi Ridge: "Taozhi Ridge"
translations.idiomatic: On "Minister of Works Hou Andu defeated Liu Yi at Taozhi Ridge"—note:

sentences.zh: 〈侯安都傳〉

translations.literal: 〈Biography of Hou Andu〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Biography of Hou Andu〉

sentences.zh: 作「桃枝嶺」。

translations.literal: reads "Taozhi Ridge."
translations.idiomatic: reads Taozhi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 以平南將軍華皎為南湘州刺史 錢大昕《廿二史考異》云：「本傳但云湘州刺史，『南』字疑衍。」

translations.literal: Appointing General Who Pacifies the South Hua Jiao as Inspector of South Xiangzhou—Qian Daxin's Examination of Discrepancies among the Twenty-two Histories says: "The main biography only says Inspector of Xiangzhou; the character 'South' is suspected to be intrusive."
translations.idiomatic: On "appointing General Who Pacifies the South Hua Jiao inspector of South Xiangzhou": Qian Daxin holds the biography reads only Xiangzhou inspector and that South is probably intrusive.

sentences.zh: 辛酉有彗星見 「辛酉」上《南史·陳世祖紀》有「六月」二字，此脫。

translations.literal: On xinyou day a comet appeared—comment: above in the Basic Annals of Emperor Shizu in the History of the Southern Dynasties there are the two characters "sixth month"—here omitted.
translations.idiomatic: On "xinyou day a comet appeared": the Southern Dynasties Annals of Chen Emperor Wen place sixth month before xinyou; it is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 按《隋書·天文志》，陳天嘉六年六月辛酉，有彗長可丈餘。

translations.literal: Comment: according to the Treatise on Astronomy in the Book of Sui, in the sixth month of Tianjia year 6 of Chen, on xinyou day, there was a comet more than a zhang in length.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Treatise on Astronomy records a comet over a zhang long on xinyou of the sixth month, Chen Tianjia year 6.

sentences.zh: 臨川太守駱文牙斬周迪 錢大昕《廿二史考異》云：「本傳及陳寶應傳但稱『駱牙』。」

translations.literal: Linchuan Governor Luo Wenya beheaded Zhou Di—Qian Daxin's Examination says: "The main biography and the Biography of Chen Baoying only call him 'Luo Ya.'"
translations.idiomatic: On "Linchuan governor Luo Wenya beheaded Zhou Di": Qian Daxin notes the biographies call him only Luo Ya.

sentences.zh: 若其經綸

translations.literal: As for their ordering the realm
translations.idiomatic: As for their governance of the realm

sentences.zh: 〔王〕業 據南監本及《元龜》一九一改。

translations.literal: [Wang] enterprise—according to the Southern Supervisory edition and Yuan Gui 191 it is changed.
translations.idiomatic: On [Wang] enterprise: emended per the Southern Supervisory edition and Yuan Gui 191.

sentences.zh: 何世無才 「才」《元龜》一九一作「之」。

translations.literal: What age lacks talent: "talent"—Yuan Gui 191 reads "it."
translations.idiomatic: On "what age lacks talent": Yuan Gui 191 reads it for talent.

sentences.zh: 按作「之」義長。

translations.literal: Comment: reading "it" gives the longer sense.
translations.idiomatic: Note: it makes better sense.

sentences.zh: 猶行杞宋之

translations.literal: Still practiced the rites of Qi and Song
translations.idiomatic: Still observed the rites of Qi and Song

translations.literal: (omitted fragment)
translations.idiomatic: (omitted fragment)

sentences.zh: 〔邦〕據南監本及《元龜》一九一改。

translations.literal: [state]—according to the Southern Supervisory edition and Yuan Gui 191 it is changed.
translations.idiomatic: On [state]: emended per the Southern Supervisory edition and Yuan Gui 191.

sentences.zh: 性靈共惻者也 「惻」原訛「測」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Nature and spirit together were moved: "moved" was originally corrupted to "measure"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "nature and spirit alike were moved": the text originally read measure for moved; other editions are correct; emended.

sentences.zh: 其若馭朽 「其」各本作「真」。

translations.literal: As if driving rotten wood: "as if"—all editions read "truly."
translations.idiomatic: On "as if driving rotten wood": all editions read truly for as if.
